items.title: One PFCP Session Modification rebuilds the datapath once per removal IE
items.body:
## Summary

`call_datapath(..., &SessionManager::ModifySession)` is invoked once per entry in the `remove_pdrs` loop — before that entry's `session->remove()` has even been applied — once per entry in `remove_fars`, once per entry in `remove_qers`, and once more at the end. A single request with N removed PDRs, M removed FARs and K removed QERs therefore triggers N+M+K+1 separate pipeline rebuilds instead of one.

A Session Modification Request is a single atomic instruction (TS 29.244 §5.2.1): the UPF should apply all of its IEs and reprogram the datapath once. Rebuild cost is per-session and grows with the rule count, so a routine multi-rule modification becomes O(rules × IEs).

There is a second effect. CH-bit F-TEID allocation calls `pfcp_switch_inst->generate_fteid_n3()`, a monotonic never-released counter, once per `ModifySession` call — so every redundant rebuild leaks an allocation.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd ci-scripts/tests
sudo ./setup_env.sh
./run_scenarios.py --scenario rebuild_once --scenario rebuild_once_update_only -v
```

| Scenario | Expected | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| `rebuild_once` — 4 removal IEs in one request | 1 rebuild | **25** |
| `rebuild_once_update_only` — no removal IEs at all | 1 rebuild | **2** |

The second is the more diagnostic of the pair: with zero removals the in-loop calls have nothing to fire on, so the extra rebuild there is the unconditional final pass compounding with the update path — which is why the first count exceeds N+M+K+1.

- `ci-scripts/tests/upf_test/scenarios/12-rebuild_once.py`
- `ci-scripts/tests/upf_test/scenarios/13-rebuild_once_update_only.py`

## Suggested fix

Delete the three `call_datapath(..., &SessionManager::ModifySession)` calls inside the `remove_pdrs` / `remove_fars` / `remove_qers` loop bodies. Leave the `session->remove(...)` calls in those loops, and leave the single final `call_datapath(...)` untouched — it already runs unconditionally whenever BPF acceleration is enabled, so no early-exit behaviour changes. With exactly one rebuild, occurring after every remove/create/update has landed on the live session, the datapath always reflects the correct final rule set.

Related: PR #5 (the test suite).

items.title: QoS and PFCP Session Modification  defects reproduced by PR #5

labels.name: closed-loop-qos
labels.description: This label is to track the Dynamic Closed Loop QoS Feature of OAI Core Network

items.body:
PR #5 adds a PFCP/N4 integration test suite for the UPF. Against a freshly restarted UPF it
reports **22 failing checks across 12 of its 16 scenarios**, reproducing the nine defects
below. `--tag smoke` exits 0, so the harness itself is healthy — these failures are the
suite doing its job.

Descriptions here are deliberately brief. Each scenario file opens with a
`Scenario / Expected behaviour / Expected output` docstring that says what it does, what a
correct UPF would do, and what a passing run prints — that is the fuller description.

To reproduce any of them:

```bash
cd ci-scripts/tests
sudo ./setup_env.sh                              # brings up the UPF and preflights
./run_scenarios.py --scenario <name> -v
```

Restart the UPF before comparing runs (`docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml restart upf`).
Deleted sessions leak their HTB classes and class ids are a hash of (SEID, QFI), so a dirty
UPF can let `qos_rate_change` pass by luck.

---

Related: PR #5 (the test suite).

items.title: UPF keeps the PFCP sessions of an association when the same CP function sets it up again
items.body:
### Description

When the UPF receives a PFCP Association Setup Request from a CP function that is already associated, it overwrites the association but keeps every PFCP session of the old one.

`upf_n4::handle_receive_association_setup_request()` calls `pfcp_associations::add_association()`. When no peer candidate exists, `add_association()` creates a new `pfcp_association`. `store_association()` then replaces the map entry. The old association object and its session set are dropped, but its sessions stay in `pfcp_switch` with their PDRs, FARs, TEIDs and UE IP entries (`src/upf_app/app/upf_n4.cpp`, `src/upf_app/app/upf_pfcp_association.cpp`, develop 5a0a6d4).

TS 29.244 V17.9.0 clause 6.2.6.2.2 covers a Setup Request with a Node ID that is already associated. The UP function overwrites the existing association, "regardless of the Recovery Timestamp received in the request". It keeps the old sessions only if the request carries PFCP Session Retention Information and asks for them; otherwise it deletes them.

The UPF does not decode PFCP Session Retention Information, so the sessions should be deleted.

This breaks a restarted SMF. After a restart, the OAI SMF sends a new Association Setup Request and allocates CP SEIDs from 1 again. Its first new session then has the same CP F-SEID as a kept session. `pfcp_switch::handle_pfcp_session_establishment_request()` finds that existing session and rejects the request (`CAUSE_VALUE_REQUEST_REJECTED`). The SMF then sends a PDU Session Establishment Reject (5GSM cause #38) to the UE. The same happens to every new session whose CP SEID matches a kept one. The kept sessions are never deleted, because no SMF knows them any more.

### Expected behavior

After an Association Setup Request from an already associated CP function, the UPF has deleted the sessions of the old association. A new session from the restarted SMF is accepted.

### Observed behavior

The old sessions stay. A new session whose CP SEID matches one of them is rejected, and the UE gets a PDU Session Establishment Reject.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the core (AMF, SMF, UPF with the simple switch) and attach one or more UEs. We used OAI gNB and nrUE in RF simulator mode, with 4 UEs.
2. Restart the SMF container (`docker restart oai-smf`). The UPF logs `Handle SX ASSOCIATION SETUP REQUEST`.
3. Restart one UE so that it requests a new PDU session.

### Logs

UPF `oaisoftwarealliance/oai-upf:v2.2.2` (the association code is the same on `develop`, 5a0a6d4). AMF and SMF are v2.2.2 with local patches for stale UE contexts and stale PDU sessions; none of them changes PFCP association handling or SEID allocation. Before the SMF restart, the UPF has 4 sessions (UP SEIDs 0x1, 0xb, 0xd, 0xe). After the restart:

```
[14:47:55.772] [upf_n4 ] [info] Handle SX ASSOCIATION SETUP REQUEST
[14:48:26.159] [upf_app] [info] Received N4_SESSION_ESTABLISHMENT_REQUEST seid 0x1
```

The session table that the UPF prints after this request still lists the same 4 old sessions and no new one. SMF:

```
[14:48:26.159] [smf_app] [debug] Received N4 Session Establishment Response sender teid 0x1  pfcp_tx_id 15
[14:48:26.160] [smf_app] [warning] N4 Session Establishment Request for PDU Session ID 10 was rejected by UPF
[14:48:26.160] [smf_n1 ] [debug] PDU Session Establishment Reject,, 5GSM Cause: 0x26
```

The UE got no IP address.

A related point on the SMF side: the OAI SMF also sends an Association Setup Request to an already associated UPF when the NRF notifies it that the UPF registered (`smf_app::handle_nf_status_notification()` → `process_upf_profile()` → `itti_n4_association_retry`). With the deletion that TS 29.244 requires, that would delete the live sessions. That is an SMF issue and is not part of this one.

A fix follows in a pull request.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-5-5

items.title: An Update QER does not change the enforced rate, and fails silently

labels.name: closed-loop-qos
labels.description: This label is to track the Dynamic Closed Loop QoS Feature of OAI Core Network

items.body:
**Files:** `src/upf_app/user/qer_tc_user.h`, `qer_tc_user.cpp`

## Summary

`Setup()` issues bare `tc class add` for the PDU-session class, the default class, its PFIFO
child and one class per GBR/MBR QER, with no existence guard. Class ids are a deterministic
hash of (SEID, QFI) via `generate_minor_id()` — a pure hash with no counter — so a second
`Setup()` for the same session and QFI always targets the class the first one created.
`tc class add` then fails with *File exists* and the old rate and ceiling stay in place.

**The PFCP response is an accept either way.** Nothing in the signalling distinguishes
"applied" from "silently ignored", which is what makes this dangerous rather than merely
wrong.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd ci-scripts/tests
sudo ./setup_env.sh
docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml restart upf     # see note below
./run_scenarios.py --scenario qos_rate_change --scenario qos_rebuild_tc_failures -v
```

| Scenario | Expected | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| `qos_rate_change` — enforced rate after an update to 20000/40000 | 20000/40000 | **50000/100000** — unchanged |
| `qos_rebuild_tc_failures` — failed `tc` operations while applying it | 0 | **6** |

The pairing is the point. A fix that stopped the `tc` failures without actually applying the
new rate would turn one green and leave the other red.

> **Restart the UPF first.** Deleted sessions leak their classes (see the shaping-state
> issue), and because the class id is a hash of (SEID, QFI), whether a later run collides
> with leftovers depends on where the SEID counter reached. On a dirty UPF `qos_rate_change`
> has been observed to pass by luck.

- `ci-scripts/tests/upf_test/scenarios/06-qos_rate_change.py`
- `ci-scripts/tests/upf_test/scenarios/14-qos_tc_failures.py`

## Suggested fix

Track the classes a `QERTCProgram` created and give `Setup()` a delete-then-add or a
`tc class change` path for a classid that already exists, rather than an unguarded add.
Surfacing a failed `tc` invocation as an error instead of a log line would also stop this
class of defect being silent — a modification that failed to reach the data plane should not
be answered with "Request accepted".

Related: PR #5 (the test suite).

items.title: Removing a QER from a live session leaves its HTB class in place

labels.name: closed-loop-qos
labels.description: This label is to track the Dynamic Closed Loop QoS Feature of OAI Core Network

items.body:
**Files:** `src/upf_app/user/qer_tc_user.cpp`,
`src/upf_app/control/SessionProgramManager.cpp`

## Summary

A modification whose only content is a Remove QER releases nothing: the class that QER's
QFI was shaped by is still there afterwards.

Distinct from the deletion case, and from the `Setup()` guard problem, because the trigger is
different — here the session continues and only one of its flows is withdrawn, so this is
removal-during-modification rather than teardown. A fix for either of the others does not
imply a fix for this.

It also has a consequence the deletion case does not: the stale class keeps a classid derived
from (SEID, QFI), so re-adding that QFI to the same session later collides with what was left
behind.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd ci-scripts/tests
sudo ./setup_env.sh
./run_scenarios.py --scenario qer_removal_prunes_class -v
```

| Check | Expected | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| the removed QER's enforcement state | gone | **survives** |
| the surviving QER's enforcement state | intact | intact |

Both halves matter: over-removal would break a flow the CP never mentioned. The scenario
establishes a two-flow session, modifies once so both flows' state exists, confirms both are
present, then removes one QER — and the QER id is resolved from the established session, so
the request cannot silently remove a QER the session never had.

- `ci-scripts/tests/upf_test/scenarios/08-qer_removal_prunes_class.py`

## Suggested fix

On a Remove QER, delete the `tc` class for that QER's QFI and drop its `sdf_filters_map`
entry, leaving the session's other flows alone. Needs the same class-tracking as the
`Setup()`/`TearDown()` lifecycle fix, so the two are worth doing together.

Related: PR #5 (the test suite).

items.title: Shaping state survives session deletion, and QER programs are replaced without teardown

labels.name: closed-loop-qos
labels.description: This label is to track the Dynamic Closed Loop QoS Feature of OAI Core Network

items.body:
**Files:** `src/upf_app/control/SessionProgramManager.cpp` (`ModifyPipeline`),
`src/upf_app/user/qer_tc_user.cpp`

## Summary

Two halves of one lifecycle problem.

`TearDown()` detaches the BPF program but never deletes the `tc` classes `Setup()` created,
so every deleted session leaves its shaping state on the interface.

And `ModifyPipeline` constructs a brand-new `QERTCProgram` that unconditionally overwrites
`qer_programs_map_[seid]` whenever QoS is still enabled — leaking the outgoing program's BPF
skeleton, since its destructor is empty. If a modification removes all of a session's QERs
the QoS-setup branch is skipped entirely, so the old program stays alive indefinitely.

The accumulation this causes is what eventually exhausts XDP attachment; that is filed
separately, since the symptom and the fix are distinguishable.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd ci-scripts/tests
sudo ./setup_env.sh
./run_scenarios.py --scenario qos_class_cleanup -v
```

| Check | Expected | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| per-flow enforcement after deletion | released | **survives** |
| per-session shaper after deletion | released | **survives** |
| shared shaping root after deletion | still present | still present |

The shared root is asserted separately, and positively: it is created once per interface and
used by every session, so removing it would break sessions this one knows nothing about. A
scenario that merely counted what remained could not tell "the session's state was released"
from "the interface was stripped".

- `ci-scripts/tests/upf_test/scenarios/09-qos_class_cleanup.py`

## Suggested fix

Have `QERTCProgram` record the classids it created and delete them in `TearDown()`, and tear
the previous program down in `ModifyPipeline` before replacing the map entry — including on
the path where all QERs were removed and the setup branch is skipped.

Related: PR #5 (the test suite).

items.title: UPF Simple Switch: GTP-U Error Indication TX omits S=1 (TS 29.281 clause 5.1)
items.body:
OAI UPF (Simple Switch datapath) sends GTP-U Error Indication (message type 26)
with S=0 and an 8-octet header, however TS 29.281 clause 5.1 requires S=1 for Error
Indication (optional header present, Sequence Number may be ignored by the peer).
Header TEID is correctly set to 0 and mandatory IEs are correct.

A peer that validates the header may reject the message as malformed and never
run TS 23.527 §5.3.3.1 recovery.

# Details

From TS 29.281 clause 5.1 (also reflected in UPF header comments in
`gtpv1u/3gpp_29.281.hpp`):

- For Error Indication, the **S flag shall be set to '1'**.
- For Error Indication, **header TEID shall be all zeros** (failed TEID is only in
  **TEID Data I**, Table 7.3.1-1 / clause 8.3).

# Tests

Setup: OAI RAN + OAI CN5G, Simple Switch UPF (`enable_bpf_datapath: no`).
Trigger: restart `oai-upf`, then UE UL with stale N3 outgoing TEID.

See:

[EI-OAICN5G.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32094267/EI-OAICN5G.zip)

```
30 1a 00 0c 00 00 00 00          flags 0x30 (S=0), type 26, len 12, TEID 0
10 00 00 00 1e                   TEID-I = 0x1e
85 00 04 c0 a8 46 81             Peer Address = 192.168.70.129
```

# Possible cause

`upf_n3::report_error_indication()` (simpleswitch/simple_switch.cpp) sets header TEID 0 and mandatory IEs, but never sets a sequence number.

`gtpu_l4_stack::send_indication()` (gtpv1u/gtpv1u.cpp) only calls msg.set_sequence_number(sn) if get_sequence_number() is true. With no SN, encode keeps S=0.

items.title: BPF rule-map entries are never pruned, on modification or on deletion

labels.name: closed-loop-qos
labels.description: This label is to track the Dynamic Closed Loop QoS Feature of OAI Core Network

items.body:
**Files:** `src/upf_app/control/SessionProgramManager.h`, `SessionProgramManager.cpp`

## Summary

`CreatePipeline` and `ModifyPipeline` only ever call `Update()` on `rules_match_pdr_map`,
`eth_rules_match_pdr_map` and `sdf_filters_map`, for the PDRs and QFIs currently present in
`session->pdrs`. Nothing ever calls `Remove()` on them — not on partial removal via a
modification, and not on full session deletion in `RemoveSession`. Entries linger
permanently.

TS 29.244 §5.2.1 makes rule removal mandatory rather than advisory, and §5.2.2 treats
deletion as releasing the session's resources.

Stale entries are keyed by (pdr_id, seid) and (seid, qfi), so they cannot be matched by a
*different* session's traffic. The cost is unbounded growth of maps sized for a fixed
session count, and rules outliving the session that owns them.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd ci-scripts/tests
sudo ./setup_env.sh
./run_scenarios.py --scenario map_pruning --scenario map_pruning_on_delete -v
```

| Scenario | Expected | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| `map_pruning` — 2 PDRs and 1 QFI withdrawn by a modification | all absent, survivors intact | all three still present |
| `map_pruning_on_delete` — session deleted | zero entries for that SEID in all three maps | every entry survives |

Both scenarios assert the rules were installed *before* removing them. That precondition is
load-bearing: removing a rule that was never there is a no-op, so without it "the entry is
absent afterwards" would pass while testing nothing.

- `ci-scripts/tests/upf_test/scenarios/04-map_pruning.py`
- `ci-scripts/tests/upf_test/scenarios/05-map_pruning_on_delete.py`

## Suggested fix

Add `Remove()` calls for the withdrawn keys on both paths: in the modification handler for
the rules the request removed, and in `RemoveSession` for everything the session installed.
Two paths, so a fix for one does not imply the other — hence the two scenarios.

Related: PR #5 (the test suite).

items.title: A Create PDR is rejected unless the same request also carries a Create FAR

labels.name: closed-loop-qos
labels.description: This label is to track the Dynamic Closed Loop QoS Feature of OAI Core Network

items.body:
**File:** `src/upf_app/simpleswitch/pfcp_switch.cpp`,
`handle_pfcp_session_modification_request`

## Summary

For every Create PDR IE the handler demands a Create FAR IE for the referenced FAR ID *in
the same request* (~`:1126`), via a `req->pfcp_ies.get(far_id, cr_far)` that must succeed. A
PDR referencing a FAR the session already has is refused outright with
`MANDATORY_IE_MISSING`.

Per TS 29.244 Table 7.5.4.2-1 a Create PDR references its FAR by ID (§8.2.74) and needs no
accompanying Create FAR. The FAR already belongs to the session; requiring it to be re-sent
makes it impossible to attach a new PDR to existing forwarding.

That blocks the pattern an SMF uses to reconfigure a QoS flow: withdraw a PDR and create its
replacement against the FAR that is already there.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd ci-scripts/tests
sudo ./setup_env.sh
./run_scenarios.py --scenario create_pdr_existing_far -v
```

| Check | Expected | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| Create PDR referencing an existing FAR | accepted | **rejected, `MANDATORY_IE_MISSING`** |
| the new PDR in the rule map | present | absent |
| **control:** the same PDR *with* a Create FAR | accepted | accepted |

The control is what makes this a diagnosis rather than a bare failure: accepted-with,
rejected-without isolates the missing Create FAR as the cause and rules out the PDR being
malformed. It is asserted rather than assumed — if the control ever failed too, rule creation
would be broken more widely and this reading would be wrong.

The scenario resolves the FAR and QER ids from the established session rather than from
constants. Rule ids are CP-assigned and session-scoped (§8.2.74, §8.2.75), so a stale
constant would reference a rule that does not exist — and the answer to that is also a
rejection, indistinguishable from the defect under test.

- `ci-scripts/tests/upf_test/scenarios/11-create_pdr_existing_far.py`

## Suggested fix

Look the FAR up in the live session first and fall back to a Create FAR IE in the same
request only when it is not already there. Reject only when neither source has it.

Related: PR #5 (the test suite).
